profile.name: Cuban motion
profile.tagline: A stylized hip rotation driven by the subtle bending and straightening of the knees.
profile.insight: Cuban motion is not a standalone dance, but a fundamental rhythmic rotation of the hips around the spine driven entirely by the knees.
profile.profile: Cuban motion is a stylized dance movement characterized by a rhythmic rotation of the hips around the spine. This rotation is caused by the bending and straightening of the knees, while the knees remain soft and slightly bent at all times. It serves as a component of American Rhythm dances. The movement tends to be easier to dance and more noticeable when the music is slow.
profile.profile_long: Cuban motion is a stylized dance movement defined by a specific mechanical execution of the lower body. At its core, the movement features a rhythmic rotation of the hips around the spine. This rotation is not initiated by the hips themselves, but is instead caused by the bending and straightening of the knees. Throughout the execution of the movement, the knees remain soft and slightly bent at all times. As a foundational technique, Cuban motion is a component of various American Rhythm dances, including bachata, mambo, salsa, rhumba, merengue, samba, and cha-cha-cha. Practitioners find that the motion tends to be easier to execute and is significantly more noticeable when performed to slow music.
